name: Core lanczos (8-bit PIL path)
plain: common_upscale's lanczos goes through 8-bit PIL images. It multiplies by 255, clips to 0..255, casts to uint8, resizes, divides by 255. That suits images in 0..1. On latents, which have negative values and a range past 1, it destroys data, so it is not a latent method despite being reachable through common_upscale.
math:
img = clip(255·x, 0, 255).uint8
img = PIL.resize(img, LANCZOS)
out = img/255

providers.author: ttulttul
providers.note: detects lanczos on latents and swaps to bicubic with a warning, src/latent_upscale_advanced.py:43

label: from code
surprise: Any pack passing "lanczos" for a latent to common_upscale clips negatives to 0 and quantises to 8 bits, comfy/utils.py:1134. FlowMatching-Upscaler guards against it; JTriggerFish lnl routes through the VAE instead (see entry).
